# Panopticlick

> Free browser fingerprinting test and privacy education project. Panopticlick shows how uniquely identifiable your browser is, simulates the real-time bidding (RTB) auctions that monetize your data, and teaches you how to defend against tracking. Independent project, not affiliated with the Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF).

Analysis starts locally in your browser. Nothing is sent for storage without explicit consent; opted-in sessions use salted IP hashes and expire after 30 days, while de-identified fingerprint aggregates expire after 90 days.

## Tools

- https://panopticlick.org/ : Browser fingerprint test — measures your browser's uniqueness in bits of entropy and estimates its advertising value.
- https://panopticlick.org/simulation/rtb/ : RTB auction simulator — runs a simulated real-time bidding auction on your fingerprint with DSP bids and CPM prices.
- https://panopticlick.org/tests/webrtc/ : WebRTC leak test — checks whether WebRTC exposes your real IP address, even behind a VPN.
- https://panopticlick.org/tests/dns/ : DNS leak test — checks whether your DNS queries bypass your VPN and reach your ISP.
- https://panopticlick.org/tests/blocker/ : Ad blocker test — uses first-party bait scripts with tracker-like paths to measure which filter rules fire, without contacting real trackers.
- https://panopticlick.org/tests/hsts/ : HSTS supercookie demo — interactive demonstration of tracking that survives cookie clearing.
- https://panopticlick.org/simulation/cname/ : CNAME cloaking explainer — how trackers disguise themselves as first-party subdomains.
- https://panopticlick.org/simulation/cookie-sync/ : Cookie syncing explainer — how ad networks share your identity via ID bridging.

## Educational guides

- https://panopticlick.org/anatomy/fingerprinting/ : Canvas, WebGL, and audio fingerprinting explained.
- https://panopticlick.org/anatomy/supercookies/ : HSTS, favicon cache, and ETag supercookies explained.
- https://panopticlick.org/anatomy/behavior/ : Behavioral tracking via mouse, keyboard, and scroll patterns.
- https://panopticlick.org/defense/hardening/ : Step-by-step browser hardening guide for Firefox, Chrome, and Brave.

## Methodology

- https://panopticlick.org/methodology/ : Full methodology with sources and limitations.
- Uniqueness is measured as Shannon entropy summed across fingerprint components (canvas, WebGL, audio, fonts, screen, navigator); "1 in N" uniqueness is 2^entropy and is an upper bound that assumes component independence.
- Entropy priors are a hand-curated probability table derived from published research (EFF Panopticlick / Eckersley 2010, INRIA AmIUnique / Laperdrix et al. 2016, Princeton WebTAP / Englehardt & Narayanan 2016), not from traffic measured on this site.
- Advertising valuations are modeled simulations: fictional DSP profiles with base CPM rates from published industry ranges (~$1-15 CPM by vertical) plus ±10% random variance. No real bid requests are sent.
